# Lab 8.12: Create an Access Level

## What We Are Going to Do
Create an access level that only matches requests from your current IP address, ready to use with IAM conditions, IAP and VPC Service Controls.

## Steps

1. **Find your access policy.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud access-context-manager policies list --organization=ORG_ID</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   If none exists, create one:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud access-context-manager policies create \
  --organization=ORG_ID --title="org-policy"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Find your public IP.** Open `https://ifconfig.me` in your browser and note the address.

3. **Write the access level spec.** Create `office.yaml`, replacing the IP:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • YAML
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">- ipSubnetworks:
  - 203.0.113.10/32</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **Create the access level.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud access-context-manager levels create office_ip \
  --title="Office IP" \
  --basic-level-spec=office.yaml \
  --combine-function=AND \
  --policy=POLICY_ID</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Look at it in the console.** Go to **Security → Access Context Manager**. You see `Office IP` with its condition.

6. **Use it in an IAM condition.** Grant Bob a role only when he connects from that IP.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
  --member=user:bob@YOUR_DOMAIN \
  --role=roles/storage.objectViewer \
  --condition="expression='accessPolicies/POLICY_ID/accessLevels/office_ip' in request.auth.access_levels,title=office-only"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Access level conditions in IAM are enforced for services that support them, such as IAP-protected resources.

7. **Keep the access level** for the IAP and VPC Service Controls labs.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Access policy | One per organization |
| Basic level | IP, region, device and identity conditions |
| Reuse | Same level works in IAP, VPC-SC and IAM |
| Device conditions | Need Endpoint Verification or Chrome Enterprise |
